description: No per-meter usage and no community series for 38 days, 2023-04-26 to 2023-06-02. Values are blank, not zero or estimated. May 2023 has no usage data and June 2023 has 28 days.

From 2023-03-20 to 2023-07-02 (105 days) metered usage is almost nil (daily totals 0.004 to 8.6 kWh), and no payments were recorded from 2023-04-26 to 2023-07-02. See Tariffs_and_Events (supply interruption, Apr to Jul 2023).
35,214 of 142,450 meter-days (24.7%) are zero. The share rose from 18.8% in 2020 to 28.6% in 2024. A zero can mean no consumption, a switched-off meter or no supply; the data does not say which.

12 runs of 3 or more consecutive days with an identical site total (83 days, flagged stale_repeated_total), and 8,334 non-zero meter-days (7.8%) that repeat the meter's previous-day value exactly (478.0 kWh). The share was 1% to 3% in 2020 to 2022 and about 12% to 14% in 2023 to 2025. These look like carried-forward readings.

On the 927 days with both (2022-06-06 to 2025-01-25) the community series totals 16,494.6 kWh and the sum of meters 13,537.4 kWh, so the meters under-count by 17.9%. The community series is higher on 798 days, never lower, and equal on every day from 2024-09-19. By year the meters reach 69% (2022), 85% (2023) and 90% (2024) of the chart. Per-meter data for 2020 to mid-2022 has no chart to compare with and probably under-counts too. The community series is the site-level total measured at the site data concentrator. An independent export of the daily energy at the site data concentrator (362 days, time stamps 2024-01-29 to 2025-01-24 at 17:00) gives identical values to the community series on every one of those days, 4,659.8 kWh in total, once its dates are aligned (+1 day, as for the community series; dataset dates 2024-01-30 to 2025-01-25). For those 362 days the sum of the per-meter readings is 4,259.6 kWh, 8.6% below the site total. This is in addition to the by-year figures. The export does not state the cause. Operator observations (first-hand): the air conditioning of the enclosure that houses the batteries and inverters was never metered, so its load is in the site total but not on any customer meter, and the operator observed customers stealing electricity and bypassing the meter. The export does not allow the gap to be split between these two, so the size of each share is not known.

The dataset contains daily values only. No hourly, 15-minute or other sub-daily data exists in the export, so load profiles within the day cannot be derived from it. No PV generation, battery or voltage data is included. The operator outage log covers December 2020 to November 2021 only (Reliability_Outages); no outage log or reliability index exists for other periods.

topic: Class labeling: blanks treated as residential
description: 230 of 248 customer codes are residential and 18 are non-residential. In the source customer file 108 customers were labeled RES, 18 BUS or INS (merged into non-residential) and 119 had no class; the dataset authors treated the 119 customers with no class, and the 3 customer codes that appear only in payment records, as residential. The source does not state that these customers are residential, so the residential group includes an assumption. By meter-days, 87% belong to meters of residential customers (including the 2 meters with no linked customer) and 13% to non-residential. Class is the status at the export date.
33 meter-days exceed 4.2 kWh (the platform's configured spike threshold); the maximum is 10.27 kWh. No obvious corruption was found, so they are kept and flagged (meter_spike_over_4.2kWh).

Customer links are the status at the export date. 133 meters have readings; the customer-to-meter link may differ from earlier years. 2 meters with readings have no linked customer. The 142 customer-meter pairs are listed in Meter_Customer_Link (see C28).

The customer file has no history. Class is the value at the export date; the snapshot is undated. The customer file also holds an energy price field, which is not included (see Caveats C23). Year created is available; closure or churn dates are not.

The operator states NGN 165 per kWh until July 2023, NGN 350 per kWh from July 2023 and about NGN 500 per kWh from February 2024. The exact start days of the changes are not recorded, and billing at each rate is not separately dated in the export. Sales agents were charged a lower rate than customers. The energy price field of the customer file is not included in this dataset: customers were not split between the 350 and 500 rates, and the values in that field are not concurrent prices. See the Tariffs sheet for the structured records.

PAY is credit bought through agents (NGN 7,499,650 across 19,769 payments). It is not the value of energy used, and NGN per kWh ratios mix the two. Types UCU and REV are adjustments. NBA and SUB records are excluded (see Data_Dictionary).

All dates are local dates in UTC+01:00 (West Africa Time). The platform's own revenue chart groups payments by UTC day; our local-date totals agree with it exactly on 92.8% of days and the UTC-day totals on 94.5%. Payments made between 23:00 and 24:00 UTC fall on the next local day here.

Meter readings 2020-08-26 to 2025-01-25. Payments 2020-07-17 to 2025-01-26. Community series 2022-06-06 to 2025-01-25. Site_Daily covers 2020-08-26 to 2025-01-25, so its PAY total (NGN 7,422,750) is NGN 73,900 plus NGN 3,000 lower than the Payments total (NGN 7,499,650). The system was energized in July 2020 (testing 2020-07-17 to 2020-07-29; first billing reading 2020-07-30). Meter_Uptime covers 2020-08-26 to 2026-10-24 (communications uptime only).
Metered use falls through 2024 while the share of zero meter-days rises. The data does not explain the fall.

Customer names, phone numbers, references, SIM numbers, coordinates, balances and the real identifiers were removed, and no customer price column is included. Year created, class and the number of linked meters remain. The smallest class group is 18 customers (non-residential). By year created, 2022 (4 customers) and 2025 (1 customer) are smaller than 5, and some combinations of class with year created or with linked meters are smaller than 5; the 3 customer codes that appear only in payment records form a group of 3. See the README for group sizes. Meter_Customer_Link joins two pseudonymous codes and holds no other attribute.

The community series is higher than the sum of the per-meter readings (see C05). Operator observations (first-hand): the air conditioning of the enclosure that houses the batteries and inverters was never metered, so its load is in the site total but not on any customer meter, and the operator observed customers stealing electricity and bypassing the meter. The export does not allow the gap to be split between these two. The gap shrinks over time and is not visible in the available data after 2024-09-19; the cause of the gap is not determined. For 2024-01-30 to 2025-01-25 the per-meter sum is 8.6% below the site total measured at the site data concentrator; the gap cannot be split between the unmetered air conditioning load and the observed electricity theft and meter bypassing.

Documents give 136, 140, 144 and 150 kWh for the battery bank. Site_Description shows all four values and uses 136 kWh (earliest as-built description) as the reference value. None has been verified by a capacity test.

Site_Description and Equipment values are taken from operator documents, not from measurements or an inspection. Design-only items (pre-construction drawings and bills of quantities) differ from the as-built system and are labeled design only. Missing values are blank.

202 (peak total customers, Dec 2020 and Jan 2021), 208 (2021 customer export), 220 (meters purchased), 245 (accounts in the current customer file, cumulative since 2020) and 232 or 240 (planning or later form figures) count different things and are not directly comparable. Site_Description lists each with its definition.

Actual build cost is the project cost breakdown (NGN 35,071,810.50). USD values use a fixed rate of 350 NGN per USD (the 2019 rate used in the source), not the rate on the purchase dates. The grouping into categories is the data owner's. The 2019 pre-construction estimate (NGN 42,463,440 at 360 NGN per USD) is design only. Costs are not adjusted for inflation or later additions.

No site-level operating cost ledger exists. OPEX contains the lines that exist: one operating-cost figure (USD 28 per month, 2023), company-account lines for grid maintenance and direct materials (2022 to 2024), and two one-off 2022 costs. Labor and metering platform fees have no recorded value and are blank. Company-account lines are not split by site.

NGN 165 per kWh applied until July 2023; NGN 350 per kWh applies from July 2023; about NGN 500 per kWh applies from about February 2024. The exact start days are not recorded and billing at each rate is not separately dated in the export, so payments around the change dates cannot be assigned to a rate with certainty. Sales agents were charged a lower rate than customers. The energy price field of the customer file is not included in this dataset: customers were not split between the 350 and 500 rates, and the values in that field are not concurrent prices. See the Tariffs sheet.

The fault log covers December 2020 to November 2021 (17 events). Later outages are not logged. For events 4, 10 and 11 the recorded duration does not match the start and end times; both values are shown and neither was corrected.

Monthly indices are as computed in the operator report for 8 months with logged outages. The reported ASAI divides the monthly SAIDI by 8,760 hours (a whole year), so it understates monthly unavailability; a recalculated monthly value is shown beside it. Months with no logged outage have blank indices. Indices describe customers served at the time, which changed over the period.

logged_outage_flag in Site_Daily marks the dates of the 17 logged events (and the following date for the 2 events that continue past midnight). It is blank outside 2020-12-01 to 2021-11-30 and 0 means only that no event is logged. Outage days outside the log period can partly be inferred from the platform data (days with near-zero site kWh, few meters reporting, or no recorded payments, as in data_flag), but no such inference is made in the flag.

topic: Meter uptime: communications only, to October 2026
description: Meter_Uptime holds six consecutive uptime reports of the management platform, 2020-08-26 to 2026-10-24, with 134 meters in each. Only communications uptime has values; power uptime and overall uptime are n/a for every meter and window, so this is not power availability, electricity availability or outage data. The mean communications uptime of meters with a value is 77.9% (window 1), 87.1% (2), 79.5% (3), 60.0% (4) and 51.7% (5). Window 6 (2026-02-16 to 2026-10-24) is n/a for all meters. Blanks: 41 meters in window 1, 35 in window 2 and 14 in window 3. A value of 0.00 is a reported zero and can mean the meter did not communicate in the window, for example because it was not yet installed or was switched off; the report does not say. Uptime coverage extends to October 2026, but usage and payments end in January 2025, so uptime cannot be compared with usage after January 2025. The calculation method is not documented.

Three meter counts appear in this dataset because they count different things. 142 is the number of customer-meter pairs: the customers with a linked meter (the meters_linked_count values in Customers add up to 142), listed in Meter_Customer_Link. 133 is the number of meters with daily readings (Meter_Daily; Site_Description). 134 is the number of meters in Meter_Uptime, which are the 133 meters with readings plus RMG01-M0134, a meter with no daily readings and no linked customer. The counts relate as follows. Of the 142 linked meters, 131 have daily readings (meter_has_readings = yes) and 11 have none (no): 142 = 131 + 11. Of the 133 meters with readings, 131 have a linked customer and 2 (RMG01-M0080 and RMG01-M0132) have none: 133 = 131 + 2. 134 = 133 + 1. The 11 linked meters without readings are in neither Meter_Daily nor Meter_Uptime; their codes RMG01-M0135 to RMG01-M0145 continue the numbering after RMG01-M0134, were assigned in the order of the linked customer codes, and are used only in Meter_Customer_Link. The links are the status at the export date and may differ from earlier years. Class agrees between Meter_Daily and Customers for all 131 pairs where both exist.

topic: Site total and sum of meters from 2024-09-19
description: Data observation: from 2024-09-19 the community series and the sum of meters in Site_Daily agree within 0.00001 kWh on all 129 days (2024-09-19 to 2025-01-25); they are identical to six decimal places on 11 of the 129 days.
